# Boolean

*JavaScript*

Methods of JavaScript booleans, `true` and `false`. `Boolean(value)` converts any value: `false`, `0`, `NaN`, `''`, `null` and `undefined` give `false`, everything else `true`.

```js
Boolean('no'); // true, as !!'no'
```

Avoid `new Boolean(false)`: it is an object, and every object counts as true in a condition.

## Methods

### constructor {#constructor}

::: member

The `Boolean` function. `Boolean(value)` converts a value to a boolean.

**Returns** `Function`

:::

### toString {#tostring}

::: member

Converts the boolean to text.

```js
(1 > 0).toString(); // 'true'
```

**Returns** [`string`](/scripting/js/String) — `'true'` or `'false'`

:::

### toSource {#tosource}

::: member

Non-standard Rhino method: returns source code that creates the value as a `Boolean` object.

```js
(true).toSource(); // '(new Boolean(true))'
```

**Returns** [`string`](/scripting/js/String) — the source code

:::

### valueOf {#valueof}

::: member

Returns the primitive value of a `Boolean` object.

```js
new Boolean(false).valueOf(); // false
```

**Returns** [`boolean`](/scripting/js/Boolean) — the primitive boolean

:::
